title: Paediatric first aid and accidents
description: Who must hold a paediatric first aid certificate, and what to do and record when a child has an accident. Based on section 3 of the EYFS statutory framework.

lessons.title: Paediatric first aid and first aiders

questions.prompt: Who must be on the premises and available at all times when children are present?

options.text: At least one person with a current paediatric first aid certificate
The manager, whether or not they hold a first aid certificate
A first aider only when children are playing outside
Any member of staff who has read the first aid policy

questions.explanation: At least one person with a current paediatric first aid (PFA) certificate must be on the premises and available at all times when children are present. They must also go with children on outings.

learnMore.title: EYFS statutory framework for group and school-based providers
HSE guidance on choosing a first aid training provider

questions.prompt: A paediatric first aider does not need to go on outings, as long as one stays at the setting. True or false?

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: False. The person with a current PFA certificate must accompany children on outings, as well as being on the premises whenever children are present.

questions.prompt: How often must paediatric first aid training be renewed?

options.text: Every year
Every three years
Every five years
Only when the setting is inspected

questions.explanation: PFA training must be renewed every three years. It must be a full course that suits people caring for young children and babies.

HSE guidance on choosing a first aid training provider

questions.prompt: A member of staff gained a level 3 qualification in 2020. Within what time must they get a PFA qualification to be counted in the staff:child ratios?

options.text: Within three months of starting work
Within one year of starting work
Before their first day
Only if the manager asks them to

questions.explanation: Staff who gained a level 2 or level 3 qualification since 30 June 2016 must get a PFA qualification within three months of starting work to be included in the required ratios. A few exceptions apply, for example for a disability, so ask your manager.

learnMore.title: EYFS statutory framework for group and school-based providers

questions.prompt: Settings should display staff PFA certificates, or make them available to parents and carers, or share a list of staff with a current certificate. True or false?

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: True. Providers should display staff PFA certificates, or make them available to parents and carers, or a list of staff who have a current certificate.

learnMore.title: EYFS statutory framework for group and school-based providers

questions.prompt: A child has a small fall and you give first aid. What must the setting do about parents and carers?

options.text: Tell them on the same day, or as soon as reasonably practicable after, and tell them about any first aid given
Wait for them to ask at the next parents' evening
Tell them only if the child needs to go to hospital
Nothing, as long as the child seems happy

questions.explanation: Providers must keep a written record of accidents or injuries and first aid treatment, and inform parents and carers of any accident or injury on the same day, or as soon as reasonably practicable after, and of any first aid given.

learnMore.title: EYFS statutory framework for group and school-based providers

questions.prompt: A child is seriously injured while in the setting's care. Within how many days must the registered provider tell Ofsted?

options.text: Within 14 days, but as soon as reasonably practicable
Within 6 months
Only if the parents complain
By the end of the term

questions.explanation: A registered provider must tell Ofsted (or the childminder agency) of any serious accident, illness or injury to a child, and the action taken, as soon as reasonably practicable and in any event within 14 days. The provider must also tell local child protection agencies.

questions.prompt: Mia, aged 3, trips on the step and bumps her head. She cries but settles quickly.

choices.text: Fetch the paediatric first aider, who checks Mia and gives any first aid
choices.feedback: Right. Get a trained first aider to her straight away.

choices.text: Give her a hug and carry on, as she seems fine
choices.feedback: She may need checking. Always ask the first aider.

choices.text: Phone her parents before anyone has looked at her
choices.feedback: Parents must be told, but first make sure Mia has been looked at.

steps.text: Mia has been checked and is happy. Pick-up time is at 5pm. What happens next?

choices.text: The accident and first aid are written down, and her parents are told the same day
choices.feedback: Yes. A written record is needed, and parents must be told the same day or as soon as reasonably practicable after.

choices.text: You tell her parents next week if they ask
choices.feedback: Parents must be told the same day or as soon as reasonably practicable after.

choices.text: You tell her parents but do not write anything down
choices.feedback: Providers must keep a written record of accidents, injuries and first aid treatment.

questions.explanation: Get a trained first aider to the child, then keep a written record and tell parents or carers the same day, or as soon as reasonably practicable after.

learnMore.title: EYFS statutory framework for group and school-based providers

questions.prompt: Your nursery has a trip to the park planned this morning. The only staff member with a current PFA certificate has called in sick.

choices.text: Make sure someone with a current PFA certificate goes with the children, or change the plan
choices.feedback: Right. A person with a current PFA certificate must go on outings.

choices.text: Go anyway, and take the first aid box
choices.feedback: A first aid box is needed, but it does not replace a person with a current PFA certificate on the outing.

choices.text: Go anyway, and ring the setting if there is an accident
choices.feedback: Someone with a current PFA certificate must be with the children on the outing.

questions.explanation: A person with a current PFA certificate must accompany children on outings. If nobody is available, the outing needs to change.
